messages:
ryan_sales: Quick heads up — Helixa POC on Dedicated (eu-west) is seeing slow time-to-first-token (~800-1200ms). Expected ~120-200ms. This started after we flipped them to the burst config + increased client concurrency. Need swarming. Also they asked if this affects cost/pricing.

maria_cs: On it. Can someone from runtime and SRE help? @alex_eng @tanvi_sre

alex_eng: Do we have a sample request_id + logs from their run? Two quick suspects: large batch wait times or cold KV/prefix cache misses. Also check if model variant was automatically downgraded/quant fallback.

ryan_sales: Pasted a single-line log from their smoke test: `2026-03-20T15:02:11.234Z request_id=helixa-req-001 queued_time=5ms batch_wait=400ms model=redwood-v1-8k quant=4bit cache_hit=false first_token=980ms`

alex_eng: batch_wait=400ms is the giveaway — runtime accumulated a large batch. cache_hit=false confirms warmup/KV miss. Are they using a single SDK connection with many concurrent streams? That often causes head-of-line batching.

tanvi_sre: Also check node metrics (cpu steal/io wait) but batching backlog is likeliest. Can somebody confirm client concurrency and socket config?

luis_support: Reached out to Helixa — they say they're spawning 16 concurrent streams from one app host using our SDK defaults.

alex_eng: If client concurrency is high + single connection, requests queue into a big batch. Short-term mitigations: lower client-side `max_batch_delay` (e.g., 8ms), reduce `max_batch_tokens`, or enable `prefer_latency` routing so runtime prioritizes small batches. Also advise a KV/prefix warmup.

ryan_sales: They'll ask about pricing: will moving to `prefer_latency` or reducing batch size increase costs?

maria_cs: Yes — less batching means less efficiency. Rough estimate: +10–20% token cost for their workload at our current throughput; I'll run exact numbers with pricing.

tanvi_sre: Quick workaround we can recommend now: run a KV warmup and tweak client settings. Example commands: `redwoodctl warmup --prefix invoice: --count 50` and set `client.batch.delay_ms=8` on their SDK. That combo usually drops first-token to ~150-250ms for similar workloads.

alex_eng: Also check model pinning — if they fell back to a slower execution path we should pin them to the verified variant and avoid automatic quant fallback during the POC.

deploy-bot: deploy: rolled redwood-runtime v2.14.3 to eu-west at 2026-03-20T15:05Z — no expected disruption.

ryan_sales: Passing suggested commands to customer now, scheduling a call for a screenshare. Will update in ~1h. :thumbsup:

maria_cs: I'll set up a 30-min screen share with Helixa — invite sent.

ryan_sales: Thanks team — if the warmup + batch tweak doesn't cut it we'll schedule an async perf trace with a runtime engineer.
